topic.title: Food: The Story in Sustainable Community Kitchens

candidate_instructions: Read all five sections. Answer Questions 1-5. Follow the stated word limits exactly.

sections.heading: How it starts
sections.text: In 2018, Grace Otieno works in a big market in Nairobi, Kenya. Every evening she sees good food in the bins. The sellers cannot sell it, so they throw it away. Grace is angry about this. One evening she takes some vegetables home. She cooks a big pot of stew. She gives the food to eight children on her street.

sections.heading: The kitchen today
sections.text: Today Grace has a small kitchen next to the market. People call it Upendo Kitchen. The word upendo means love. The kitchen cooks hot food for 300 people every week. The food is free. Grace does not buy any vegetables. The sellers in the market give her the food they cannot sell.

sections.heading: A day in the kitchen
sections.text: The day starts early. At six o'clock, two helpers walk around the market with big baskets. They collect onions, beans, rice and fruit. At nine o'clock the cooking starts. There are three big pots. At twelve o'clock the kitchen opens. People come with their own bowls. The kitchen closes at two o'clock.

sections.heading: The helpers
sections.text: Twelve people work at Upendo Kitchen. Only Grace gets money for her work. The other eleven people are volunteers. Some of them are mothers of the children. One volunteer is a nurse. She comes on Friday. She talks to people about healthy food. The volunteers wash the pots too.

sections.heading: Problems and plans
sections.text: Grace has two problems. In the rainy season there is not much fruit in the market. Then there is not enough food for everybody. The kitchen is also very small. Grace wants a bigger room and a new cooker. In 2027 she wants to open a second kitchen in another part of the city.

passage.full_text:
Paragraph 1 — How it starts
In 2018, Grace Otieno works in a big market in Nairobi, Kenya. Every evening she sees good food in the bins. The sellers cannot sell it, so they throw it away. Grace is angry about this. One evening she takes some vegetables home. She cooks a big pot of stew. She gives the food to eight children on her street.

Paragraph 2 — The kitchen today
Today Grace has a small kitchen next to the market. People call it Upendo Kitchen. The word upendo means love. The kitchen cooks hot food for 300 people every week. The food is free. Grace does not buy any vegetables. The sellers in the market give her the food they cannot sell.

Paragraph 3 — A day in the kitchen
The day starts early. At six o'clock, two helpers walk around the market with big baskets. They collect onions, beans, rice and fruit. At nine o'clock the cooking starts. There are three big pots. At twelve o'clock the kitchen opens. People come with their own bowls. The kitchen closes at two o'clock.

Paragraph 4 — The helpers
Twelve people work at Upendo Kitchen. Only Grace gets money for her work. The other eleven people are volunteers. Some of them are mothers of the children. One volunteer is a nurse. She comes on Friday. She talks to people about healthy food. The volunteers wash the pots too.

Paragraph 5 — Problems and plans
Grace has two problems. In the rainy season there is not much fruit in the market. Then there is not enough food for everybody. The kitchen is also very small. Grace wants a bigger room and a new cooker. In 2027 she wants to open a second kitchen in another part of the city.
